scope: Stage8 independent static code review: GameplayRuntimeSession, GameSystem.Session adoption, Controller aliases/rollback/replacement, three new tests

findings.description: stopped is checked only on Pump entry. Dispose invoked by an in-flight tick or scheduled command does not stop remaining catch-up callbacks, because UnityLogicalLoop.Dispose only removes the Editor subscription and passed tick/canAdvance remain unguarded.
findings.recommendedFix: Guard advancement and tick delivery on runtime stopped state, without a render-frame guard or discarding normal pending frames; add stop-from-tick and stop-from-command regressions.
findings.status: resolved: UnityLogicalLoop final disposed state blocks public advancement/scheduling and stops command/input-command continuations and Drain; queue references released without resetting Clock/debt

checked: Existing UnityLogicalLoop object and pre-Start construction timing retained.
Runtime creates Input/Random/Logger and receives Core via existing Controller factory arguments.
Pump restricts driver and rejects re-entry while preserving normal multi-frame catch-up.
Initialization retry relinquishes loop disposal ownership before managed/local session teardown.
Manager replacement synchronizes Runtime, Controller alias and GameSystem.Session at the existing timeline boundary.
UnityInputProvider.Dispose is idempotent for repeated Controller rollback cleanup.
Dialogue and exploration-resume loops remain outside this runtime cut.
limits: Final compile, related472 and full3580 are pending at review time; reviewer executed no Unity operations/tests.
Loop.Dispose is now terminal; legacy integration checks must confirm no legitimate code reuses a disposed loop. Startup retry intentionally avoids disposing it.
Planned HUD regeneration identity proof is not arbitrary world/battle hot reload support.

checked: Stop from scheduled command halts remaining same-frame commands and tick.
Stop from tick prevents subsequent catch-up frames.
Timestamped input-command continuation checks disposed after each callback.
Normal undisposed catch-up still uses existing Drain with no render-frame suppression.
Clock object/frame/pending debt preserved at final Dispose.
ReturnLoopForInitializationRetry relinquishes disposal ownership, preserving retry loop.
reReview.newRegression: Two cases assert tick/command stop, no later callbacks, Frame1/Pending5, and direct Advance remains stopped.
